sources.markdown: A binary heap is a complete binary tree in which every parent is no larger than its children.
Inserting into a heap takes O(log n) time.

beat.say: A heap is a tree where every parent is smaller than or equal to its kids.

sources.markdown: The sample has 25 students, and their mean score is 78 points.

beat.say: Twenty five students took part, and they averaged 78 points.

sources.markdown: Quicksort picks a pivot and partitions the array around it. Its average running time is O(n log n).

beat.say: Quicksort picks a pivot, then splits the array around it. Fast on average: n log n.

sources.markdown: A hash table maps keys to slots using a hash function.
Two keys that land in the same slot are called a collision.

beat.say: A hash function sends each key to a slot. When two keys share a slot, that is a collision.

sources.markdown: The sample has 25 students, and their mean score is 78 points.

beat.say: Twenty five students took part, and they averaged 87 points.

sources.markdown: Quicksort picks a pivot and partitions the array around it.

beat.say: Quicksort always runs in linear time, so it beats every other sort.

sources.markdown: A larger sample size makes the standard error smaller.

beat.say: A larger sample makes the standard error bigger.

sources.markdown: A binary heap is a complete binary tree in which every parent is no larger than its children.
Inserting into a heap takes O(log n) time.

beat.say: Inserting into a heap takes log n time.

sources.markdown: The mean of a data set is the sum of its values divided by how many values there are.

beat.say: Add up all the values, then divide by how many there are. That is the mean.

sources.markdown: A p-value is the probability, assuming the null hypothesis is true, of seeing a result at least as extreme as the one observed.

beat.say: Assume the null is true. The p-value is how likely a result this extreme would be.

sources.markdown: A stack is a last-in, first-out structure. Push adds an item to the top and pop removes the top item.

beat.say: A stack is last in, first out. Push adds on top. Pop takes the top one off.

sources.markdown: Binary search halves the remaining range on each step, so it needs at most about log2 n comparisons.

beat.say: Binary search cuts the range in half every step. So it needs about log n comparisons at most.

sources.markdown: About 95 percent of values in a normal distribution lie within two standard deviations of the mean.

beat.say: In a normal distribution, about 95 percent of values sit within two standard deviations of the mean.

sources.markdown: Every recursive function needs a base case that stops the recursion, and a recursive case that moves toward it.

beat.say: A recursive function needs a base case to stop. And each recursive step must move toward that base case.

sources.markdown: A multiplexer has 2 data inputs, one select input and one output. The select input chooses which data input reaches the output.

beat.say: A multiplexer has two data inputs and one select. The select picks which input reaches the output.

sources.markdown: Variance is the average of the squared differences from the mean.

beat.say: Variance is the average of the squared distances from the mean.

sources.markdown: Merge sort splits the list in half, sorts each half and merges the sorted halves.

beat.say: What if sorting a list just meant splitting it, sorting both halves, and merging? That is merge sort.

sources.markdown: The central limit theorem applies when the sample is large enough, often taken as at least 30 observations.

beat.say: The central limit theorem needs a big enough sample. A common rule of thumb is at least 30.

sources.markdown: Hash tables give average constant time lookups.

beat.say: Hash tables always give constant time lookups, no matter what.

sources.markdown: Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths from one source in a graph with non-negative edge weights.

beat.say: Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths even when edge weights are negative.

sources.markdown: A queue is a first-in, first-out structure.

beat.say: A queue is first in, first out, and it was invented in 1952 at Bell Labs.
